bettman-nature-preserve.mobility.1: Bettman Nature Preserve also boasts a small nature preserve, and a paved wheelchair accessible path leading to views of the preserve.
bettman-nature-preserve.sensory.1: Bettman Sensory Garden and Pathway – Located in O’Bryonville, this historical outdoor space provides a series of accessible walkways, easy access to an overlook, an accessible picnic table and raised planting beds.
bettman-nature-preserve.cognitive.1: The library and archives are open to the public by appointment; our volunteer staff is available on Tuesdays from noon to 3pm. For more information on Bettman Nature Center, please call 513-321-6070. Hours: Currently closed to the public. Open for programming only.
bettman-nature-preserve.chronic.1: Hours: Currently closed to the public. Open for programming only.
licking-river-greenway-trails.mobility.1: Covington's trail includes 1.5 miles of nature trail, .75 miles of paved trails, and approximately 2.5 miles of trail utilizing sidewalk and road infrastructure.
Trail access can be found behind Holmes High School at the corner of Levassor and Eastern Ave. Additional locations to access the trail include the dead end of E. 16th Street, Clayton-Meyer Park and behind Randolph Park.
licking-river-greenway-trails.mobility.2: Most of that stretch includes parallel trails – about 0.75 miles of paved trail atop the levee and about 1.5 miles of a gravel “nature trail” that cuts through a narrow stretch of woods along the river’s edge.
All told, the LRGT is 2.5 miles long, including sidewalk and road infrastructure.
